written: 2026-11-14, before running a2_parpola.py on any data
unit: distinct M77 texts (distinct()), break-free runs; dev split for development, heldout + ICIT non-M77 sites for confirmation

sign_sets.note: M103 (3 as 2-over-1) excluded from '3' because shaunmortal F7 shows it is bound to M403; M99/M100 (2 short) excluded as connective (F7)

claims.source: Parpola 1994 ch.10-14: numeral+fish = asterisms; aru-min 'six stars' = Pleiades, elu-min 'seven stars' = Ursa Major, mum-min 'three stars' = Mrgasiras
claims.prediction: Among short-numeral tokens, the probability that the next sign is a fish (M59 or marked fish) is higher for 6 and 7 (and 3) than for the other values; 6+fish and 7+fish are over-represented relative to (numeral frequency x fish share after numerals). Null: P(fish|n) is the same for every n (permutation of follower labels across numeral tokens).
claims.falsified_if: 6 and 7 are not above the pooled rate, or their excess is no larger than that of non-asterism values (1,4,5,8,9,12)

claims.source: Parpola: marked fish = compound words built on min (mey-min roofed fish = Saturn, etc.)
claims.prediction: Marked fish signs occupy the same slots as plain fish: their left/right neighbour distributions and relative-position profile are closer to M59's than those of frequency-matched non-fish signs (null: 1000 random frequency-matched signs).
claims.falsified_if: similarity to M59 not above the 95th percentile of matched signs

claims.source: Parpola: different marks = different words (different stars/deities), not scribal variants
claims.prediction: Marked fish and plain fish co-occur in the same text (as in lists of star/deity names) at least at the rate expected from their frequencies; allographs of one sign would be expected to avoid co-occurrence or stand in free variation with identical contexts.
claims.falsified_if: co-occurrence of plain and marked fish within texts is significantly BELOW independence (avoidance) AND contexts are indistinguishable

claims.source: Parpola semantics (derived by us, not stated by him as a corpus prediction)
claims.prediction: If marked fish are names of single planets (Saturn etc.), numerals should precede marked fish less often than plain fish ('seven stars' is a name, 'seven Saturns' is not).
claims.falsified_if: numeral-before rate for marked fish >= plain fish

claims.source: Mahadevan (1970s-2000s): the terminal 'jar' M342 is a Dravidian masculine singular suffix -an ('the one of')
claims.prediction: (a) M342 is text-final far above chance; (b) as a suffix it attaches to many different preceding signs: left-neighbour type diversity of M342 is above frequency-matched signs; (c) it alternates in the final slot with a small set of other final signs after the SAME preceding sequence (paradigm), more than shuffled texts.
